lead: Epilepsy is the commonest neurological disorder in pregnancy. Most women have normal pregnancies; the risks come from fits and from antiepileptic drugs.
f: About two thirds: no change · About one third fit more, mostly those poorly controlled before · Why: vomiting and missed doses, poor sleep, falling drug levels (lamotrigine most) · Fits are commonest in labour and the first days after birth

sc: More fits at 30 wk on lamotrigine → Levels fell: raise the dose

f: Differential: eclampsia (over 20 wk or within 48 h of birth, high BP, proteinuria), cerebral malaria, hypoglycaemia, meningitis, cerebral venous thrombosis, low sodium · Maternal: injury, aspiration, pre-eclampsia, anaemia (folate), depression, status epilepticus, SUDEP · Fetal: miscarriage, anomalies (drugs), FGR, preterm birth, hypoxia in long fits

sc: Known epileptic fits at 36 wk with BP 160/110 → Treat as eclampsia: MgSO₄

f: Major anomaly risk about 6–8% with one drug, 8–16% with several · Valproate: neural tube defect (1–2%), heart, cleft, low IQ: avoid if she may conceive · Carbamazepine: NTD about 1%, cleft; enzyme inducer · Phenytoin: fetal hydantoin syndrome (cleft, nail and finger hypoplasia) · Phenobarbitone: heart, cleft, neonatal drowsiness · Lamotrigine: lowest risk

sc: Cleft lip, small nails, short fingers → Phenytoin

f: Plan pregnancy; ideally fit-free for 2 years; one drug, lowest dose; switch from valproate before conception · Folic acid 5 mg from 3 months before conception · Never stop drugs suddenly: status epilepticus is more dangerous · Continue the same drugs; levels not routine · Anomaly scan, fetal echo, growth scans; BP and urine each visit · Enzyme inducers: vitamin K 1 mg IM to the baby at birth

sc: 7 wk pregnant on carbamazepine, fit-free → Continue it; folic acid 5 mg

f: A fit over 5 min or repeated fits without recovery · IV lorazepam; hypoxia threatens mother and fetus

Hospital birth; induction about 38 wk; vaginal birth (CS for obstetric reasons) · Continue drugs (IV if vomiting); avoid exhaustion and dehydration · Early epidural; avoid pethidine (its metabolite causes fits) · Breastfeeding encouraged; a dose raised in pregnancy returns to the old dose within 10 days · Screen for depression · Baby safety: feed and change on the floor, never bathe alone

tr: Enzyme inducers make the combined pill, POP and implant fail: use a copper IUD, LNG-IUS or DMPA
The combined pill lowers lamotrigine levels and brings fits back
